newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: New Lithuania govt reaffirms reform, Western ties.
newsitem.headline: New Lithuania govt reaffirms reform, Western ties.

text.p: Lithuania's new right-wing government said on Thursday it would keep the country firmly on the path of economic reform and continue to seek stronger ties with the West as it unveiled its draft programme to parliament.

The Homeland Union, headed by independence hero Vytautas Landsbergis, swept to victory in parliamentary elections last month and has formed a coalition government with the right-wing Christian Democrats.
"We will seek the earliest possible membership in the European Union (EU) and NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation)," said the draft programme, obtained by Reuters.
The small Baltic state, which quit the former Soviet Union six years ago, is keen on gaining membership in both organisations to shield it from a potentially hostile Russia.
"Reforms should be decisive, and implemented until the end," the programme said.
"Legal and financial programmes, which encourage long-term business and financial investment, should be implemented.
"All subsidised prices and tariffs should be abolished by the middle of 1998," the programme said.
